ChatExport.description:
Structured summary of a conversation, ready to be formatted into a note.

One flat model rather than a discriminated union, because `mode` must
default to "summary" when the client omits it and a pydantic discriminated
union requires the tag to be present. Fields that do not belong to the
selected `mode` are rejected by app/services/chat_export.py — inside the
tool body, so the rejection travels through _McpCall's GatewayError
conversion instead of the SDK's raw ToolError path.

`related_notes` carries only the client's candidate paths — it is not what
gets rendered. app/services/related_notes.py re-verifies every path
against the Vault (this model cannot: it has no filesystem access), and
app/services/chat_export.render_chat_export takes the verified survivors
through a separate `verified_related_notes` argument, never this field
directly. See docs/adr/0006-verified-related-note-wikilinks.md.

context.description: technical mode only. The problem or constraints the design starts from.
context.title: Context

conversation_type.description: Optional. A short free-form label for the kind of conversation, e.g. 'design', 'debugging', 'review'. Omit it rather than guessing.
conversation_type.title: Conversation Type

decisions.description: Only conclusions that were actually adopted or choices that were explicitly agreed. Not options still under discussion, and not things left to do — those belong in unresolved_issues and next_actions, never here. Leave empty when nothing was decided.
decisions.title: Decisions

definitions.description: reference mode only. Term and meaning pairs.
definitions.title: Definitions

design.description: technical mode only. The design or approach itself, one point per item.
design.title: Design

environment.description: issue mode only. Versions, hosts, configuration relevant to the problem.
environment.title: Environment

examples.description: reference mode only. Concrete examples, one per item.
examples.title: Examples

facts.description: reference mode only. Standalone facts worth looking up later.
facts.title: Facts

implementation_notes.description: technical mode only. Details that matter when implementing: file names, function names, gotchas.
implementation_notes.title: Implementation Notes

investigation.description: issue mode only. What was checked and what it showed, in order.
investigation.title: Investigation

key_points.description: summary mode only. The points worth remembering, one per item.
key_points.title: Key Points

mode.description: Which export shape to render. Use 'summary' for a plain 'summarise this and save it' request and whenever no other mode clearly fits. 'technical': a design or implementation discussion. 'history': how something changed over time. 'full': a long conversation covering several distinct topics. 'procedure': repeatable steps someone will follow later. 'issue': a problem, its investigation, and its cause. 'reference': terms, facts, and examples to look up later.
mode.title: Mode

next_actions.description: Concrete things someone will do next, one per item. Keep this separate from unresolved_issues — a task is not an open question, and the two must never be merged. Leave empty when there is nothing to do next.
next_actions.title: Next Actions

overview.description: summary mode only. What the conversation was about, in a few points.
overview.title: Overview

prerequisites.description: procedure mode only. What must already be true before starting.
prerequisites.title: Prerequisites

project.description: Optional. The project or repository this belongs to, when the conversation names one. Omit it rather than guessing.
project.title: Project

related_notes.description: Vault-relative .md paths of existing notes this conversation relates to — call search_notes first and pass paths exactly as it returned them; never invent or guess a path. Usually 3-5 items, at most 10. The Gateway re-verifies every path when writing the note: a path it cannot verify is left out rather than blocking the export, so the rendered '## 関連ノート' section — not this input — is the record of what actually got linked.
related_notes.title: Related Notes

rollback.description: procedure mode only. How to undo it if it goes wrong.
rollback.title: Rollback

root_cause.description: issue mode only. The established cause. Leave empty when the cause was not established — do not put a guess here.
root_cause.title: Root Cause

sources.description: Where the information came from: a URL, a document name, a command that was run. One per item.
sources.title: Sources

steps.description: procedure mode only, and required for it. One action per item, in the order they must be performed. Rendered as a numbered list; do not put your own numbering in the text.
steps.title: Steps

symptom.description: issue mode only, and required for it. What was observed going wrong — the behaviour, not the cause.
symptom.title: Symptom

tags.description: Open-ended Obsidian tags you choose for this note. No fixed vocabulary. Write them without a leading '#'; spaces are replaced with '-'. title, created, updated, source and export_mode are generated by the Gateway and cannot be set here.
tags.title: Tags

timeline.description: history mode only, and required for it. Events in the order they happened, oldest first.
timeline.title: Timeline

tldr.description: Required. Normally 2-5 short sentences covering the subject, the conclusion, and the current state. One sentence per item; they are joined into a single paragraph directly under the title.
tldr.title: Tldr

topics.description: full mode only, and required for it. One entry per distinct topic the conversation covered, in the order they came up. Each becomes a '###' subsection.
topics.title: Topics

turning_points.description: history mode only. The moments where the direction actually changed.
turning_points.title: Turning Points

unresolved_issues.description: Questions still open: things not yet decided or not yet known. Keep this separate from next_actions — an open question is not a task, and the two must never be merged. Leave empty when nothing is open.
unresolved_issues.title: Unresolved Issues

verification.description: technical and procedure modes only. How to confirm it works: tests, commands, expected output.
verification.title: Verification

workaround.description: issue mode only. What makes it usable without a full fix.
workaround.title: Workaround

DuplicateCandidate.description:
One existing inbox note that may already cover the same conversation.

No absolute path, note body, or excerpt — only what is needed to decide
between creating a new note and appending to this one. ``score`` is
intentionally not exposed: it is an internal sort key
(docs/adr/0007-*.md), not a stable contract a client should depend on.

'confirm': exactly one high candidate and nothing else at high/medium — ask the user to choose new/append/cancel. 'choose': more than one high/medium candidate, or only medium ones — show the candidate list and require an explicit pick. This is advisory, not write authorization: the Gateway never blocks or gates create_inbox_note/append_inbox_note on this value.

ErrorCode.description:
The error code vocabulary (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN section 13).

Two codes need a note:

* ``RATE_LIMITED`` is part of the published contract but is never raised in
  Phase 1 — no rate limiting is implemented yet.
* ``VALIDATION_ERROR`` is an addition to section 13's list (which the plan
  calls "主なエラーコード", i.e. non-exhaustive). Request validation failures
  that are not about a path or a title — a non-integer ``limit``, an unknown
  body field — need a code of their own rather than being forced into
  ``INVALID_PATH``.
ErrorCode.title: ErrorCode

InboxNoteCreateRequest.description:
Exactly one of `content` or `export` is required; sending both, or
sending neither, is rejected. `export` and `frontmatter` are also
mutually exclusive — `export`'s frontmatter (title/created/updated/
source/export_mode/tags) is formatter-owned and cannot be supplied as
arbitrary free-form frontmatter alongside it. `content`/`frontmatter`
remain the raw-Markdown path kept for existing callers; `export` is the
structured chat-export path (issue #12 / docs/adr/0005-*.md).

content.description: Markdown body. Written as-is with LF line endings. Exactly one of `content` or `export` is required.
content.title: Content

export.description: Structured chat-export input (issue #12). The Gateway renders this into deterministic Markdown and frontmatter; the client never supplies raw Markdown or frontmatter alongside it. Exactly one of `content` or `export` is required.

frontmatter.description: Optional YAML frontmatter for the `content` path. Scalars and flat lists of scalars only. Rejected together with `export`, whose frontmatter is formatter-owned.
frontmatter.title: Frontmatter

title.description: Human-readable title. The file name is derived from it by the API; callers cannot choose a path.
title.title: Title

info.description: Read-mostly gateway over an Obsidian vault: full-vault search, note reads, vault tree/summary browsing, inbox duplicate-candidate detection, and note creation and append restricted to 00_Inbox/ChatGPT. MCP (mounted at /mcp) is the primary interface; this REST API is kept for health checks, curl-based diagnostics, and regression tests. Every failing response uses the single `{"error": {"code": ..., "message": ...}}` envelope described on each operation below — never FastAPI's default `{"detail": ...}` shape.
